title: Drugs that act on the reward pathway, and the classes we file them under

links.label: The commercial side of this: the audacity of bupropion

figures.note: one radar per compound, spokes are percentiles within the set. the xanthines share a shape. the weight-loss row shares none.
licensed class by colour. the weight-loss set spans the whole plot; the stimulants sit on top of each other.
density of the same space. one peak, under the polar surface area where drugs reach the brain.

line: why a weight-loss drug keeps turning up in addiction research, for anyone scouting repurposing candidates: 24 compounds licensed for five different things, plotted by the chemistry they share
question: GLP-1s turn out to blunt addictive behaviour. Bupropion treats both weight and smoking. ADHD is a disorder of impulse. If these drugs all touch the reward pathway, do the classes medicine files them under survive contact with the molecules?
calls: sampled by what each drug is licensed for, not by scaffold. sampling on structure would presuppose the answer.
percentile rank on the radar spokes, not min-max. one peptide is twenty times the mass of everything else.
XLogP against TPSA rather than a fingerprint embedding. both axes can be checked by a reader; an embedding only looks impressive.
semaglutide kept, on a log axis. a small amine and a peptide inside one licensed class is the whole observation.
withdrawn drugs kept in. keeping only the survivors removes the contrast.
broke: enantiomer pairs return identical 2D descriptors from PubChem and land on one point. merged into single markers, so the clinical difference between them is invisible here.
tried: scaled the radar spokes with min-max first. every small molecule collapsed onto the same dot beside the peptide, so switched to percentile rank within the set.
did: sampled 24 compounds by what they are licensed for, across xanthines, stimulants, wakefulness agents, non-stimulant ADHD drugs and weight-loss drugs, rather than by scaffold.
pulled computed molecular properties for each from PubChem and plotted the licensed classes against the chemistry.
checked which classes hold together in property space and which scatter.
found: the xanthines share a shape on the radar. Caffeine, theophylline and theobromine behave as one family on every spoke.

the weight-loss row shares none. Phentermine, orlistat and semaglutide are licensed for the same thing and have nothing chemical in common, which is the clearest sign that the licence is not a chemical category.
bupropion sits with the non-stimulant ADHD drugs by licence while being the molecule that also carries smoking and weight indications. The class it is filed under does not predict where it gets used.
so_what: a licensed class is a regulatory artifact, not a mechanism. Screening repurposing candidates by indication will miss the compounds that cross classes, which are exactly the interesting ones.
the compounds that scatter in property space while sharing a behavioural effect are the ones worth a mechanistic look. That is the shortlist this chart produces.
not_shown: the reward-pathway target network behind this framing is not built yet; this card currently shows the chemistry, not the mechanism
